title: Remove unnecessary length check for container hostname ID
body:
**Summary**

Since container IDs are validated to always be exactly 64 characters long upon creation, the `< 11` length check when determining the short ID hostname is dead code. 

This PR removes the unnecessary boundary check and unconditionally returns the truncated 12-character ID `c.ID()[:12]`.

Hi, in my unrelated change I also needed the short ID and was about to add one more instance of `c.ID()[:12]`.

I remembered seeing this PR and wanted to ask here if it would make sense to have a `shortID()` method as there are quite a few instances (11?) of truncating the ID inline.

(I first added that, but then realized I was wrong and didn't actually needed that myself.)

> I remembered seeing this PR and wanted to ask here if it would make sense to have a shortID() method as there are quite a few instances (11?) of truncating the ID inline.

I am not sure it is worth it, in many places we just have [:12] inline, adding an extra function import everywhere for this one thing might not be worth it. But I would object it either.

> > I remembered seeing this PR and wanted to ask here if it would make sense to have a shortID() method as there are quite a few instances (11?) of truncating the ID inline.
> 
> I am not sure it is worth it, in many places we just have [:12] inline, adding an extra function import everywhere for this one thing might not be worth it. But I would object it either.

Sure, it looked like the method should be available everywhere (Docker/Moby has a [function](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/8430f1e347c785f5a2cd412e2f3e2fba55c33882/client/pkg/stringid/stringid.go#L29) for that) and would get inlined by the compiler anyway. It seemed more self-documenting to me, but just a very minor thing I noticed.
